event.title: Highest temperature in London on July 29?

eventMetadata.context_description:
**High pressure building across southern England is driving trader consensus toward a peak of 32–33°C in London on July 29, with Met Office guidance indicating a maximum of 33°C under mostly sunny skies and light winds.** 

Recent model runs show warm southerly flow advecting air from the continent, supporting daytime highs several degrees above the July average of ~22–24°C, consistent with the ongoing warm spell across southeast England. Minor forecast spread arises from differences in predicted cloud cover timing, boundary-layer mixing, and the strength of the urban heat-island effect in central London, which can add 1–2°C locally. Official agencies such as the Met Office and ECMWF continue to converge on dry, stable conditions with little risk of significant cooling until later in the week, leaving the outcome sensitive to the final 24–48 hours of model updates. Traders therefore assign the highest implied probabilities to the narrow 32–34°C band while assigning low odds to extremes below 30°C or above 35°C.

The resolution source for this market will be information from Wunderground, specifically the highest temperature recorded for all times on this day for the Munich Airport Station, available here: https://www.wunderground.com/history/daily/de/munich/EDDM.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the gear icon next to the search bar and switch the Temperature setting between °F and °C.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Celsius (eg, 9°C). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent ensemble forecasts from major numerical weather prediction models position the 32–34°C range as the most probable peak for Munich on July 29, reflecting a transient ridge of high pressure and warm advection from the south. Official guidance from the German Weather Service and European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts shows daytime highs stabilizing near these values amid partly cloudy skies and light winds, with limited convective cooling expected. This aligns with the broader 2026 European heat episode, where observed anomalies have exceeded seasonal norms by 5–8°C in southern Germany. Updated model runs over the next 48 hours will refine boundary-layer details and any late-day cooling, directly influencing trader consensus on the exact daily maximum.
